guide_title: New to FPV? What you need for a build
guide_lead: A quad needs the five parts below. Pick one size and keep every part in that size: the 3-inch and the 5-inch builds use different boards, frames and motors. Each name opens that exact part. The flight controller and ESC (the stack) are paid stock; the other parts are funding targets.
guide_role_fc: The onboard computer. It keeps the quad stable and turns your stick commands into motor commands.
guide_role_esc: Takes battery power and drives the four motors. Take the same size as the flight controller.
guide_role_frame: The carbon body. Everything else bolts onto it.
guide_role_motors: One motor per arm, so a quad needs four.
guide_role_receiver: Picks up the commands from your radio and passes them to the flight controller.
guide_also_title: You will also need (not sold here)
guide_ships: Batch 1 of the flight controller and ESC is paid for and {stack_ships}.
guide_when_body: The frame, motors and receiver each have a funding target and ship about 10 weeks after it is reached. One order ships in one parcel when its last item is ready, so if you want the flight controller and ESC in October, order them on their own. Each order pays its own shipping.
guide_add_waits: The {parts} are funding targets. Add them now and the whole parcel waits for them, or order the stack now and the rest later (shipping is paid again).
guide_dji_title: Flying DJI goggles? Which radio to get
guide_dji_body: Your DJI goggles work with a DJI O3 or O4 air unit on the OpenFrame: the air unit is the camera and video transmitter in one. The OpenFrame also takes analog, Walksnail and HDZero video systems, each with its own goggles.

The OpenRX receiver needs a radio with an ExpressLRS transmitter. Simplest: a radio with 2.4 GHz ExpressLRS built in, so no extra module. A radio with a module bay and an ExpressLRS module also works. A DJI remote controller or motion controller does not use ExpressLRS and cannot control the OpenRX.

Keep the radio and the receiver on the same ExpressLRS major version before binding. Binding pairs the receiver with your radio: you set the same binding phrase on both, or put the receiver in bind mode and press Bind on the radio. The quick-start card in the box shows the steps.
help_whoop: There are no whoop-size parts. The smallest OpenDrone build is 3-inch: [see what a 3-inch build needs](/products#build-3-inch). The OpenRX Lite below is a 10.0 × 11.5 mm ExpressLRS receiver with a CRSF output and a 5 V input.
help_video_radio: We do not sell goggles, radios, cameras or video transmitters. Your goggles pair with the video system on the quad: a DJI O3 or O4 air unit works with DJI goggles, analog with analog goggles. The OpenFrame takes analog, DJI, Walksnail and HDZero video systems. The OpenRX receivers need a radio with an ExpressLRS transmitter; a DJI remote controller cannot. [Which radio to get, and how binding works](/products#coming-from-dji).
help_size: OpenDrone makes 3-inch and 5-inch parts. There is no 7-inch or long-range frame yet: the largest build is the [5-inch build](/products#build-5-inch). For a longer radio link, the OpenRX Mono and Gemini add a sub-GHz band.
help_gps: OpenDrone does not sell a GPS module. See [what a build needs](/products#new-to-fpv).

guide_receiver_swap: Have a 900 MHz radio module? Pick the [Mono or Gemini](/products/openrx?Model=Gemini) instead.
guide_also_3inch: A radio with 2.4 GHz ExpressLRS. Simplest: ExpressLRS built into the radio, so no extra module.
A LiPo battery and a charger for it.
To fly through the camera: an FPV camera and video transmitter (or one digital air unit), and goggles. The frame takes analog, DJI, Walksnail and HDZero video systems.
A soldering iron, solder and flux: a build is soldered together.
guide_also_5inch: A radio with 2.4 GHz ExpressLRS. Simplest: ExpressLRS built into the radio, so no extra module.
A LiPo battery and a charger for it.
To fly through the camera: an FPV camera and video transmitter (or one digital air unit), and goggles. The frame takes analog, DJI, Walksnail and HDZero video systems.
A soldering iron, solder and flux: a build is soldered together.
help_spare: Every part is sold on its own, so a crashed quad needs only the broken part: each flight controller and ESC size, each frame and single motors. The warranty covers defects, not crash damage: see [Warranty](/warranty).
help_gift: Buying for someone else? The flight controller and ESC ship from late October 2026; the other parts ship by 11 March 2027 or you get a refund. The order can go to the recipient's address. [Buying as a gift](/preorder#gift).
